1_fp_growth_mining.reason: FP-Growth on transactions creates a sparse one-hot matrix. With ~20,000 baskets and ~4,000 products, mlxtend executes fast (< 2s) when min_support >= 0.01. However, setting min_support < 0.002 will blow up the frequent itemset tree and risk out-of-memory on 8 GB Unified RAM.
1_fp_growth_mining.bottlenecks: RAM exhaustion if min_support is configured too low (< 0.005).
1_fp_growth_mining.recommended_configuration: Keep min_support >= 0.010 (1.0%) and filter to top 1,000 frequent items if scaling up.

2_daily_demand_forecasting_xgboost.reason: Resampling to daily granularity generates ~365 time-series observations. Feature matrix (lags, rolling means, calendar features) is compact (< 400 rows x 15 columns). Training on 8 CPU cores takes under 200 ms.
2_daily_demand_forecasting_xgboost.bottlenecks: Dataset historical depth (1 year = 365 daily points); cannot fit multi-year seasonal cycles.

3_weekly_demand_forecasting_xgboost.reason: Aggregating to weekly granularity yields 51 data points. The dataset is extremely lightweight. XGBoost trains instantaneously on CPU.
3_weekly_demand_forecasting_xgboost.bottlenecks: Low sample count (51 points). After 8 lag steps, only 43 training/test instances remain.
3_weekly_demand_forecasting_xgboost.recommended_configuration: XGBRegressor(n_estimators=60, max_depth=3, learning_rate=0.08) to prevent overfitting.

4_individual_product_level_forecasting.reason: Training models for top 10 - 20 individual high-volume products is fast and feasible. However, attempting to train 4,000 separate XGBoost models in a synchronous loop would take 30+ minutes and create excessive CPU thrashing.
4_individual_product_level_forecasting.estimated_resource_requirements: RAM: ~500 MB | Runtime: 5 - 15 seconds (for top 5-10 products)
4_individual_product_level_forecasting.bottlenecks: Zero-sales intermittency (intermittent demand) for low-velocity catalog items.
4_individual_product_level_forecasting.recommended_configuration: Restrict dedicated forecasting models to the Top 5 to 10 selling products with continuous sales.

5_hyperparameter_tuning_cross_validation.reason: Expanding-window rolling-origin cross-validation with a moderate grid (e.g., 30 - 50 parameter combinations) runs smoothly on 8 CPU cores in < 30 seconds. A brute-force grid with > 1,000 combinations or nested CV is unnecessary and not recommended.
5_hyperparameter_tuning_cross_validation.bottlenecks: CPU core contention if running parallel n_jobs=-1 alongside Next.js and IDE.
5_hyperparameter_tuning_cross_validation.recommended_configuration: Use TimeSeriesSplit(n_splits=4) or expanding origin with 36 parameter trials, n_jobs=4.

6_neural_network_gpu_experiments.reason: Apple M2 has unified memory with Metal 4, but lacks NVIDIA CUDA/Tensor Cores. XGBoost on macOS does not have Metal acceleration and runs strictly on CPU. Furthermore, for 51 weekly points or 365 daily points, deep learning (e.g. LSTM, Transformer, N-BEATS) is mathematically unjustified, severely prone to overfitting, and adds huge overhead.
6_neural_network_gpu_experiments.estimated_resource_requirements: RAM: > 3.0 GB | Runtime: Minutes to Hours (PyTorch MPS/CPU)
6_neural_network_gpu_experiments.bottlenecks: Lack of CUDA, extreme overfitting risk on small tabular time-series.
6_neural_network_gpu_experiments.recommended_configuration: Stick with tree-based Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and statistical baselines.
